question: What is the typical temperature range of a mercury-based clinical thermometer?
solution:
The correct answer is __35°C to 42°C__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Mercury-based clinical thermometers__ are designed to measure human body temperature.
 
• The typical temperature range is 35°C to 42°C, suitable for detecting body temperature.
 
• This range ensures accuracy in diagnosing fever or hypothermia.
 
• They are sealed glass tubes containing mercury, which expands with heat.
 
• Mercury thermometers are highly precise, but they must be handled with care due to the toxicity of mercury.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Digital Thermometer:**

 
 
• Digital thermometers are an alternative to mercury thermometers and are safer to use.
 
• They provide quick and accurate readings using electronic sensors.
 
 
 
• **Infrared Thermometer:**
 
 
• Infrared thermometers measure temperature from a distance without contact.
 
• They are commonly used to measure surface or forehead temperature.
